✅ **Prompt Updated**: Showcase Key Sheet (showcase_key_sheet)

Updated prompt: showcase_key_sheet

📜 **Version 2** saved (use `action:"history"` to view)

**Changes**: +6 additions, -4 deletions

```diff
===================================================================
--- a/development/showcase_key_sheet/prompt.yaml
+++ b/development/showcase_key_sheet/prompt.yaml
@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@
 id: showcase_key_sheet
 name: Showcase Key Sheet
-description: "Per shot, actor and plate family after the pose sheet (D72, D77, D83): generate the key sheet through the imagegen tool from the approved model sheet, the pose sheet's declarations and the shot's cards: row 1 every key of the family at model-sheet scale (cut into key plates), row 2 the same keys as frame thumbnails at the layout camera (the staging proof for C25); overlay, silhouette, spine-fit (C31) and clean-up checks per key; a world's style contract, when the shot visits one, governs row 2 only."
+description: "Per shot and actor after the pose sheet (D72, D77, D83, D85): build every key plate from the pose sheet's solved joints through its plate family's mesh at model-sheet scale, measure what the rubric contracts per key (C20 overlay, C21 silhouette, C22 contour, C31 spine fit), propose a new plate family through the imagegen tool only for a silhouette the rig cannot hold and register it by toolchain, and render the staging row at the layout camera (C25); the key gate reads the measured joints."
 category: development
 userMessageTemplateFile: user-message.md
 arguments:
===================================================================
--- a/development/showcase_key_sheet/user-message.md
+++ b/development/showcase_key_sheet/user-message.md
@@ -1,9 +1,11 @@
 Shot: {{shot}}
-Actors: {{actors | default("every actor with keys in the chart")}}
+Actors: {{actors | default("every actor with keys in the pose sheet")}}
 Production root: {{output_root}}
 Pose sheet handoff:
 {{context | default("Read the pose step's result from chain history (v3/poses/<shot>.json); a missing pose sheet is BLOCKED, run animation_poses.")}}
 
-Read `v3/creative-spec.md` (D65–D72, D74, D77, D83, Craft baseline, clean-up standard), `v3/rubric.md` (C20–C25, C31), `v3/poses/<shot>.json` (the pose contract: per key the moment, the curve class, bow and side, the weight foot, the lead arm and leg, the silhouette kind, the face state, the plate family and the solved joints; a missing or probe-refused pose sheet is BLOCKED), `v3/charts/<shot>.json` (frames and holds), `v3/layouts/<shot>.json` (the camera contract: the frame at the start and end of the move, emitter positions, the lead actor's on-screen height; a missing or unapproved layout is BLOCKED, run showcase_layout_sheet), the picks the pose sheet cites (`v3/references/owner/picks.json`, eagle ids) and each actor's `assets/<actor>/model.json` (contour standard in `contour.ratio`, D76); an actor with no approved model sheet is BLOCKED (run showcase_model_sheet). Companions are drawn from their official plates under `assets/codex` and `assets/clawd`, never from the layout sheet's loose versions; a garment transition (D69) is drawn as five flat roles, never as cloth. For each actor generate ONE key sheet per plate family through the `imagegen` tool (`tool:imagegen`): `references` are the absolute paths of the actor's model sheet, the approved pick, the shot's card files and the cited pose picks; the `prompt` lists every key of the family in order (K1…Kn: the moment, the curve in words from the declaration, which foot carries the weight, which arm and leg lead, the silhouette kind, what changes) and asks for TWO rows on one plate: ROW 1 every key as a full figure at the model sheet's scale and baseline, numbered K1…Kn left to right, pure black field, five flat colors with identity pigments by hex, pale contour at the model sheet's line (D76); ROW 2 the same keys as frame thumbnails at the layout's camera (the figure at the layout's on-screen height, the emitter where the layout puts it at that frame, the D74 hue pair as the only radiance, the leading line of the move visible), numbered F1…Fn under their keys; `out` is `out/<shot>-keys-<actor>-<family>-<NN>.png`. Row 1 is the plate that is cut; row 2 is the staging proof the render study is compared against (C25) and never cut. When the shot visits a world with its own style contract (`v3/worlds/<world>.json`, if any), row 2 is drawn in that world's line and fill language and names it; row 1 stays in the home style so the plate cuts cleanly. Then, per key: overlay it on the model sheet and report head count and limb ratios (C20, reject above 5 %); fill its silhouette black and judge whether the pose reads (C21); register the joints to the rig (`scripts/s01_keys_to_rig.py` or the skeleton toolchain of `v3/studies/tech-rig-01.md`; never estimated by hand) and measure the spine fit, bow and twinning against the pose sheet's declaration with `probe-poses.py --shot <shot>` (C31, reject a class or side that disagrees, a bow more than 0.02 under the declaration, or twinning the pose did not declare); measure contour weight, taper and closure (C22). A rejected key is regenerated once on its own plate with the failing property named in the prompt (the curve drawn in words, the limb that twinned); a second failure stays REJECTED on the sheet for the owner. Cut every accepted key into `assets/<actor>/keys/<shot>/K<n>.png` with `scripts/cutout.py --field black` (role quantization, soft alpha and contour per D71) and record sha256; write the registered joints into `v3/keys/<shot>.json` against the pose sheet's names and frames. No key is ever tweened by generation (D68). Measure row 2 against the layout: the figure's height at the start-of-move key within 5 points of the layout's, the emitter within 3 % of frame width (C25). Lay the sheet (both rows), overlays, silhouettes and the measured curve over each key into the `KeySheet` composition and render one still.
+Read `v3/creative-spec.md` (D65–D72, D74, D77, D83, D85, Craft baseline, clean-up standard), `v3/rubric.md` (C20–C22, C25, C31), `v3/poses/<shot>.json` (the contract: per key the moment, curve, weight, lead, silhouette kind, plate family and the solved joints; a missing or unsolved pose sheet is BLOCKED, run animation_poses and `npm run solve-poses -- <shot>`), `v3/layouts/<shot>.json` (a missing or unapproved layout is BLOCKED, run showcase_layout_sheet), each actor's `assets/<actor>/model.json` and plate families under `assets/<actor>/families/` (an actor with no approved model sheet is BLOCKED, run showcase_model_sheet), and `scripts/animation/README.md` §plates.
 
-Return: Keys (actor, family, id, frame, declared curve vs measured class/bow/twinning, plate path, sha256, joints registered yes/no); Frame Keys (F1…Fn: figure height vs layout, emitter vs layout, world); Model-sheet Overlay (per key); Silhouettes; Clean-up Measured; Probe Lines; Sheet Paths; Generation Receipts; Rejected Keys; Concerns.
\ No newline at end of file
+The plates are built here, not described to a generator (D85). Run `npm run plates -- <shot>`: every key is rendered from its solved joints through its plate family's mesh at the model sheet's scale and baseline on the black field (D71, D76), its joints written to `v3/keys/<shot>.json` with `source: solver`, and its measurements recorded per key: model-sheet overlay (C20: head count and limb ratios within 5 %), silhouette read (C21), contour ratio against the model sheet (C22, ±20 %), and the spine fit against the declaration (C31, `probe-poses.py --shot <shot> --joints keys`). A key the script reports as NEEDS FAMILY is a silhouette the rig cannot hold (a fold, crossed or overhead arms, a stoop): propose that family's plate once through the `imagegen` tool (`tool:imagegen`) with `references` = the model sheet, the approved pick and the cited pose cards, and a `prompt` naming the silhouette kind, the curve in words, the weight foot and the lead side, with the solved joints drawn as a guide; cut it with `scripts/cutout.py --field black`, build its mesh and register its joints with the skeleton toolchain (or the documented fit, flagged `registration: fit`), never by eye; then re-run `npm run plates`. A family plate that fails C20 or C22 is regenerated once with the failing property named; a second failure stays NEEDS FAMILY on the sheet for the owner. Row 2 of the key sheet (the keys as frame thumbnails at the layout camera, C25) is rendered from the same plates through the `KeySheet` composition, with the measured curve drawn over each key. Companions are drawn from their official plates under `assets/codex` and `assets/clawd`; a garment transition (D69) is five flat roles, never cloth. The gate runs `probe-poses.py --joints keys` over the key sheet; quote its lines.
+
+Return: Keys (actor, family, source solver|family-plate, id, frame, C20 head/limbs, C21, C22, C31 declared vs measured class/bow/sign/twinning, plate path, sha256); Families (new families proposed, how registered); Frame Keys (F1…Fn: figure height vs layout, emitter vs layout); Probe Lines; Sheet Paths; Generation Receipts (family plates only); Needs Family; Concerns.
\ No newline at end of file

```
